learning_outcomes.text: Know the basic principles governing fluid movement.
Know and apply mass, momentum, and energy balances in a control volume.
Be able to apply dimensional analysis and physical similarity in the study of models.
Be able to calculate pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Handle laboratory instruments for measuring pressure, flow, and velocity to calculate fluid systems, obtain results, and draw conclusions.
Be able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Fluid mechanics equations in integral form
Fluid mechanics equations in differential form
teaching_methods: Classroom presentations of concepts and problem-solving sessions

assessment_methods.method: Problem solving, assignments, report writing, presentation and defense of practical cases or projects

assessment_rules: The laboratory practice grade has a weight of 20% (5 lab practices + test). The average grade of the two controls OR the final exam OR the extraordinary exam will be worth 80%. The subject can be passed by continuous assessment if all 5 lab practices are completed and the grade [80% (average of 2 controls) + 20% (5 lab practices + test)] is greater than 5 points. Students who do not pass by continuous assessment must take a comprehensive final exam in the ordinary or extraordinary call, which will have a weight of 100% of the final grade.
